page_title: SSHTermaq – PuTTY-compatible SSH client for Windows and macOS

sources.entry: SSHTermaq - PuTTY-compatible SSH, Telnet and serial terminal with tabs, split panes, an SFTP/SCP file manager and one-click PuTTY session import. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/f1resh/sshtermaq) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: SSHTermaq
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source, PuTTY-compatible SSH client for Windows and macOS that adds tabs, split panes and an SFTP file manager.
use_cases: Managing several servers in tabs and split panes
Running the same command on many hosts at once
Uploading and downloading files to remote servers
Migrating saved PuTTY sessions and keys to a new client
Connecting to devices over Telnet or serial ports
Tunnelling traffic through SSH port forwarding or jump hosts
summary.what_it_does: SSHTermaq is a terminal client supporting SSH-2, Telnet, Rlogin, Raw TCP and serial connections. It adds tabs, split panes and broadcast input to PuTTY's feature set. Each SSH session has an SFTP panel, and a two-pane file manager lets you drag files between the local machine and the server, with a transfer queue and resumable transfers; it falls back to SCP when SFTP is unavailable. It imports saved sessions, default settings, trusted host keys and OpenSSH config from PuTTY or ~/.ssh/config, and supports Ed25519, RSA and ECDSA keys in OpenSSH or PuTTY .ppk format. Host keys are checked on each connection, and saved passwords are encrypted by the operating system.
notable: Imports existing PuTTY sessions, keys and host keys with no re-setup
Two-pane SFTP/SCP file manager beside the terminal
Tabs, split panes and broadcast input to multiple sessions
Licensed MIT, free with no account or ads
caveats: Runs only on Windows 10/11 (64-bit) and macOS 12 or later; no Linux version yet
GitHub installer and zip for Windows are not code-signed, so SmartScreen warns on first run
Windows version needs the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime
